Plan, not record. September 2026 has not happened. This is what the planner would do, day by day, produced by the simulator that backtested August to within a fraction of a percent. Forecast demand is marked FORECAST; every declared assumption is flagged in the data. WhatsApp messages are simulated drafts — nothing was sent, nobody replied.

Materials PLAN

What the plan starts with, what it eats, and what is left. 209 components sit under the month's 84-SKU plan; 88 of them have less than 100% month cover at the freeze, 47 must be ordered in week 1 and 41 are already late — the full cover table with order-by dates lives on Order-by. Oil synonyms are already merged (reference/oil-synonyms.csv; freeze already canonical — no alias codes present). Measured lead times: oil 11 d, packaging 6 d.

“Landed” includes the freeze's open POs arriving and the orders the sim raises during the month — it is not additive with the “On PO” column. Every landing assumes “supply arrives exactly on its lead time” ASSUMED. “Used” is oil consumed by scheduled runs; the month's total oil draw of 27,66,013 L also includes 639 L of flush oil not attributed to a single family. Needs are per base oil — merged (reference/oil-synonyms.csv; freeze already canonical — no alias codes present).

The blend simplification — declared, not hidden

Engine simplification ASSUMED

Some SKUs fill a blended oil. The engine plans blends by their recipes: their demand is decomposed into the base oils in the table above, and when the sim needs blend oil mid-month it buys and runs it under the blend's own code (LOOSE OIL GOLD, SO OLIVE OIL). What it cannot see is blend stock already standing at the freeze — ready blend on the floor on day 1 is invisible to production, so the plan orders base oil it may not strictly need and the closing figure below understates real oil by whatever ready blend existed on 31 Aug. That is a simplification of the engine, not a fact about the godown.

Read this number with its caveats
simulated It exists only if September runs exactly as planned — every landing assumes “supply arrives exactly on its lead time”. A late tanker moves it down; an unrun day moves it up.
definition This is the 13-component BOM-relevant set. The freeze's all-RM count (8,06,143 L at open) is a different, broader definition — never reconcile the two directly.
blends Ready blend standing at the freeze is invisible to the engine (note above), so real closing oil would be slightly higher than shown.
carry Treat it as October's planned opening position, not a forecast of the SAP book — the biggest single carry is mustard loose oil at 9,09,194 L.

Two different definitions, both real, both in the order-by data — two different zero definitions live in order-by-sep.json — label whichever you show. The literal-zero count here is 6 packaging and 0 oil items (deduplicated across SKUs (one SKU counted once however many zero items block it); per-item sum would be 4530289). It is smaller than the 7-item zero-shelf card above by design: 7 items open the month at on_hand exactly 0 = 6 with nothing on order (the literal-zero count) + 1 already covered by a live PO to chase. Packaging “pieces” remain mixed units throughout — a cap and a carton each count as one.

This is a forward plan, not a record. September 2026 has not happened; only the 1-September opening is observed. The factory has not run this way.
Measured: the 31-Aug stock and open POs, the open order backlog, BOMs, line speeds and clearance, realise, lead times. Assumed (declared, flagged in the data): forecast demand buckets for volume not yet ordered, the even ecom spread, supply exactly on lead time, the invoice→truck lag, the observed line-efficiency derate, the storage ceiling (open question Q2), standing stock uncounted at open. Phone numbers are masked — September has no approval to show them.
Every number traces to sim/sep-inputs.json via scripts/gen-data.py.
